subject: BridgeCraft adapter: certification & validation kickoff
messages:
From: Avery Chang <avery@bridgecraft.io>

Cc:

Subject: BridgeCraft adapter: certification & validation kickoff

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for taking this on. BridgeCraft has completed our first pass at the adapter that connects our orchestration layer to Redwood's inference API. We'd like to run a formal validation and certification so we can list Redwood as a supported runtime in our partner catalog.

What we're hoping for from Redwood: a short technical validation (compatibility, perf, and operational runbook), a reference deployment pattern for customers using our adapter + Dedicated or Private, and a lightweight certification stamp if the tests pass.

Attachments: bridgecraft-adapter-v1.zip (adapter binary + manifest), interop-specs.pdf (endpoints + expected payloads).

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood run a 48–72 hour staging soak with our adapter and share perf/latency breakdowns?
- Validation checklist: request schemas, auth patterns, model variant fallbacks, KV cache interactions, and error/fallback behaviour.
- Any required security artifacts (e.g., connector security checklist, recommended KMS/HSM patterns) we should provide?

We can provide a staging endpoint and temporary creds; our DevOps team is ready to coordinate.

Proposed kickoff window: this Thursday (2026-11-12) or next Monday (2026-11-16).

Avery
Partner Eng, BridgeCraft
avery@bridgecraft.io

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Hi Avery —

Appreciate the package and the clear asks. We can take the lead on a focused validation: compatibility, performance profiling, and an operational reference (runbook + failure modes). I'll outline a simple plan below and propose next steps.

Summary plan (draft):
- Phase 0: Intake (today–tomorrow): we validate payload schemas and auth flows.
- Phase 1: Staging soak (48 hours): run traffic that mirrors your expected customer profiles (small/medium/large sequences).
- Phase 2: Stress and edge-case tests: quantized models, long-context runs, KV cache refresh and cold-start behaviour.
- Phase 3: Readout + certification criteria: pass = no unhandled 5xxs, latency within agreed SLOs, documented operational runbook.

Perf targets (proposal):
- P50 token latency under 120ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) on Dedicated medium instances
- Error rate < 0.5% during soak
- KV cache hit rate measured and reported; cache-related stalls flagged

Sergio and Kim will own the technical validation and security checklist respectively.

Immediate asks for your team:
1) Staging endpoint + example workload URLs (you said you can provide this).
2) A short list of model variants your adapter will call and any special headers/auth flows.
3) Confirm the kickoff window — Thursday 11/12 works for our infra team at 10:00 PT.

I've attached a first-pass draft validation plan for internal alignment: bridgecraft-validation-plan-draft.md

If that all sounds good I will calendar the kickoff and loop in Jonas for the deployment runbook review.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Partner GTM (Redwood Inference)
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Avery Chang <avery@bridgecraft.io>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BridgeCraft adapter: certification & validation kickoff

Lauren —

Quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff. I pulled the adapter manifest from the ZIP and annotated a few compatibility flags we should watch for:

- Protocol: their adapter negotiates a streaming WebSocket fallback when chunked responses are required. We should validate both HTTP/1.1 streaming and WS fallback for the same workload.
- Auth: Bearer token via Authorization header; they also have a signed timestamp header for replay protection — good to validate clock skew handling.
- Model variants: they support calling multiple model families; recommend we test at least one LLM-large (32k context) and one quantized medium.
- KV cache: make sure key eviction behaviour doesn't lead to pathological re-hits during soak — we'll instrument cache hit/miss and per-request KV lookup latency.
- Error surface: adapter returns 4xx with structured error JSON; ensure Redwood's retry/fallback policy won't hide a legitimate customer error. We may need a specific rule to pass 4xx through to the client.

Test harness items I will prepare:
- Synthetic traffic generator that replays customer prompt traces (scrubbed).
- Latency and token-level breakdowns per model variant.
- Regression checks against baseline (our internal 99th percentile).

A few asks for BridgeCraft before Thursday:
1) Sample prompt sets for small/medium/large usage.
2) Clarify their intended default model for Dedicated customers.
3) If they have any preferred failure-mode responses (e.g., explicit fallback to a lighter model).

I'll attach the small checklist to the kickoff invite.

— Sergio
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
